subject: Cognitive Science
title: Exemplar Theory
description: A micro-lesson that makes Exemplar Theory usable.

hook.text: Maybe you don't store one ideal bird. Maybe you store every bird you've ever encountered.

buildup.text: Exemplar theory says categories are collections of remembered instances, not abstractions.

discovery.text: You classify a new animal by comparing it to specific dogs, cats, and birds you've actually seen.

twist.text: This explains why personal experience warps categories. A vet's "typical dog" differs from yours.

climax.text: Exemplar models beat prototypes at capturing unusual or highly variable categories.

quiz.question: How does exemplar theory differ from prototype theory?
options: It stores specific instances instead of an ideal summary
